headline: AI voice assistants can be tricked by ambient sound, researchers find
summary: New research shows AI agents can be manipulated by commands hidden in background noise or speech, with a 69% success rate in lab tests.
details: Researchers have demonstrated a new vulnerability in multimodal AI agents: they can be tricked by audio commands hidden within ambient noise or overlapping speech. This 'audio prompt injection' bypasses the usual defenses against text-based prompt attacks.

The study found that AI models like Gemini 3 Pro and GPT-4o-audio, which continuously process audio input, can be manipulated to follow malicious instructions approximately 69% of the time under lab conditions.

While this is a new modality for a known vulnerability class, it significantly expands the attack surface. Anything making a sound near a microphone could potentially be used to issue commands to an always-listening AI agent.

Despite the alarming success rate, researchers caution that this doesn't mean AI voice assistants are production-ready for exploitation. Lab conditions rarely translate directly to real-world scenarios, and specific concealment techniques were used.

A more encouraging finding is the development of a defense mechanism, cross-modal consistency detection (CADV), which achieved over 90% detection rates in the same tests. This suggests the issue is a pipeline design gap rather than a fundamental flaw.

Developers integrating multimodal agents with voice input need to treat ambient audio as untrusted, similar to how web content is handled. This includes input provenance, segmentation, and consistency checks between audio and other authorized channels.

The industry faces a challenge in balancing enhanced security with user experience. Implementing these defenses may introduce inference-time overhead and potential false positives that could annoy users.

headline_marked: [[Google Pixel 11]] lineup reportedly gets $100 price hike, RAM cuts
headline: Google Pixel 11 lineup reportedly gets $100 price hike, RAM cuts
summary: The Pixel 11 is expected to start at $899 with 256GB storage, while Pro models see RAM reduced to 12GB and increased prices.
details: New leaks suggest the entire Google Pixel 11 lineup will see a $100 price increase across the board. The base Pixel 11 is rumored to start at $899, but will offer 256GB of storage, a step up from the previous 128GB.
However, the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL are reportedly facing a RAM cut, dropping to 12GB. These models are also expected to see price hikes, starting at $1,099 and $1,299 respectively.

The standard Pixel 11 might also lose its telephoto lens, potentially settling for a dual rear camera setup. The Pro models are expected to retain a similar camera configuration to the Pixel 10 series.
Even the Pixel 11 Pro Fold is not immune to these changes, with rumors indicating it will also feature 12GB of RAM and a new starting price of $1,899.
